function.name: restaurant_finder
function.description: Search for restaurants based on location, cuisine type and other preferences. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: City and state, e.g. New York, NY.

cuisine.description: Type of cuisine the user is interested in, e.g. Italian, Japanese etc.

preferences.description: Extra features in the restaurant. default is ['Delivery'].

2) Find sushi restaurants in Los Angeles (Los Angeles, CA) that provide delivery service.

But the function's preferences param is typed as "Vegetarian" | "Delivery" | "Vegan" | "Takeout"[], but it's ambiguous: It says preferences?: "Vegetarian" | "Delivery" | "Vegan" | "Takeout"[]; That seems like it could accept either a single string or an array? But likely they intend preferences to be an array of strings from those options. We'll pass arrays.
